title: Malta, Arrival in Rome, Paul's Ministry in Rome

questions.question: After the shipwreck, all reached the island safely. What was the island called?
options: Malta
Crete
Cyprus
Melitene
questions.explanation: Acts 28:1 (ESV): "After we were brought safely through, we then learned that the island was called Malta."

questions.question: As Paul gathered sticks and put them on the fire, what attached itself to his hand due to the heat?
options: A viper
A scorpion
A water serpent
An adder
questions.explanation: Acts 28:3 (ESV): "When Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and put them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand."

questions.question: The native people of Malta saw the viper on Paul's hand. What did they initially conclude about him?
options: "No doubt this man is a murderer. Though he has escaped from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live."
"This man has angered the gods and is being punished among us."
"He must have done some terrible wrong to be bitten so suddenly."
"The gods are testing this man to see if he is truly righteous."
questions.correctAnswer: "No doubt this man is a murderer. Though he has escaped from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live."
questions.explanation: Acts 28:4 (ESV): "When the native people saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, 'No doubt this man is a murderer. Though he has escaped from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.'"

questions.question: Paul shook the viper into the fire and suffered no harm. When the people waited for him to swell up or fall down dead and nothing bad happened, what did they then think?
options: He was a god
He was protected by the gods
He was a great prophet
He had magical powers
questions.explanation: Acts 28:6 (ESV): "...they changed their minds and said he was a god."

questions.question: The chief man of Malta was named Publius. He welcomed them and who did Paul heal?
options: Publius's father, who was sick with fever and dysentery
Publius's mother who was lame from birth
Publius himself who was gravely ill with fever
The leading men of the island who were struck with disease
questions.correctAnswer: Publius's father, who was sick with fever and dysentery
questions.explanation: Acts 28:8 (ESV): "It happened that the father of Publius lay sick with fever and dysentery. And Paul visited him and prayed, and putting his hands on him, healed him."

questions.question: After Paul healed Publius's father, what happened throughout the rest of the island?
options: The rest of the people on the island who had diseases also came and were cured
The islanders gathered to hear Paul preach the gospel of Jesus Christ
The native people brought all their sick from surrounding villages
A great revival broke out and many on the island were baptized
questions.correctAnswer: The rest of the people on the island who had diseases also came and were cured
questions.explanation: Acts 28:9 (ESV): "And when this had taken place, the rest of the people on the island who had diseases also came and were cured."

questions.question: How long did they stay on Malta?
options: Three months
One month
Forty days
Six months
questions.explanation: Acts 28:11 (ESV): "After three months we set sail in a ship that had wintered in the island, a ship of Alexandria, with the twin gods as a figurehead."

questions.question: When Paul arrived in Rome and the brothers heard of his coming, where did they come to meet him?
options: The Forum of Appius and Three Taverns
The city gates of Rome near the Tiber
The harbor at Ostia when the ship docked
The Jewish synagogue on the Sabbath day
questions.correctAnswer: The Forum of Appius and Three Taverns
questions.explanation: Acts 28:15 (ESV): "And the brothers there, when they heard about us, came as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns to meet us."

questions.question: When Paul saw the Roman brothers who came to meet him, how did he respond?
options: He thanked God and took courage
He wept with joy and praised God
He raised his hands and blessed them
He embraced them and encouraged them
questions.correctAnswer: He thanked God and took courage
questions.explanation: Acts 28:15 (ESV): "On seeing them, Paul thanked God and took courage."

questions.question: In Rome, Paul was allowed to stay by himself with just one soldier guarding him. He called together the local leaders of the Jews. What was the first thing he told them?
options: He had done nothing against the Jewish people or the customs of the fathers, yet was handed over to Rome as a prisoner
He came to Rome not as a criminal but to appeal to Caesar about the resurrection
He had been falsely accused by the Jerusalem authorities and needed their help
He wished to preach the gospel of Jesus Christ to them though already a prisoner
questions.correctAnswer: He had done nothing against the Jewish people or the customs of the fathers, yet was handed over to Rome as a prisoner
questions.explanation: Acts 28:17 (ESV): "...though I had done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, yet I was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans."

questions.question: Paul explained the kingdom of God and about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets to the Roman Jews. Some were convinced by what he said and others disbelieved. As they disagreed among themselves, Paul quoted from Isaiah. The quote said God told Isaiah the people's hearts had grown dull and their ears were hard of hearing so they would not understand, lest they should turn and be healed. Paul then declared salvation had been sent to whom?
options: The Gentiles; they will listen
All who believe regardless of nation
Those whose hearts are ready to receive it
The faithful remnant of Israel first
questions.explanation: Acts 28:28 (ESV): "Therefore let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will listen."

questions.question: For how long did Paul live in his own rented dwelling in Rome, welcoming all who came?
options: Two whole years
One year
Three years
Eighteen months
questions.explanation: Acts 28:30 (ESV): "He lived there two whole years at his own expense, and welcomed all who came to him,"

questions.question: Acts concludes with a summary of Paul's ministry in Rome. He was "proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without..."?
options: hindrance
opposition
fear
restraint
questions.explanation: Acts 28:31 (ESV): "proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without hindrance."

questions.question: The ship from Malta that took them onward toward Rome had what figurehead on its bow?
options: The twin gods Castor and Pollux
A golden eagle of Rome
The goddess Isis of Alexandria
A carved image of Neptune the sea god
questions.correctAnswer: The twin gods Castor and Pollux
questions.explanation: Acts 28:11 (ESV): "...a ship of Alexandria, with the twin gods as a figurehead." Castor and Pollux (the Dioscuri) were patron gods of sailors.

questions.question: Paul's final recorded words to the Roman Jewish leaders were a quotation from Isaiah. Just before quoting Isaiah, Paul said "The Holy Spirit was right in saying to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet..." This remarkable statement implies what?
options: The Holy Spirit was the true author of Isaiah's words
Isaiah spoke with divine authority that these leaders recognized
The Holy Spirit's prophecy was now being fulfilled in their rejection
The prophet's words applied equally to their forefathers and to them
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit was the true author of Isaiah's words
questions.explanation: Acts 28:25-26 (ESV): "...the Holy Spirit was right in saying to your fathers through the prophet Isaiah: 'Go to this people, and say...'" This identifies the Holy Spirit as the divine author behind Isaiah's prophecy.

key_verse_text: proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without hindrance.
